hypothesis: the arithmetic transfer effect is the policy, not the phrasing: three pre-specified wording variants of step-calc all beat direct answering
methods: ROOT="$PYTHON_EVO_REPO_ROOT"; [ -n "$ROOT" ] || { echo "no repo root" >&2; exit 1; }; export EVO_REPO_ROOT="$ROOT"; export EVO_REPO_ROOT="$ROOT"; PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/src:$ROOT/demo/shared:$ROOT/demo/transfer" python3 "$ROOT/demo/transfer/run_prompt_ablation.py" --selftest && PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/src:$ROOT/demo/shared:$ROOT/demo/transfer" EVO_OUT="$RD/artifacts" EVO_SEED=20261011 EVO_MODELS="qwen2.5:7b,gemma3:4b,llama3.1:8b" python3 "$ROOT/demo/transfer/run_prompt_ablation.py"

kill_switch.note: all variants beat direct: the effect is the policy, report it as such
at least one variant fails: the effect is wording-sensitive, narrow the claim to the canonical phrasing

tension: Step-calc is one specific wording, and the entire transfer effect could live or die on that phrasing rather than on reasoning-before-answering as such. No arm has varied the wording while holding everything else fixed, so whether the paper's central claim describes a policy or a prompt is unmeasured. Answering it decides if the claim generalizes across phrasings or must be narrowed to the exact tested wording.
